clue.text: Insulting rebuff Harold got at Hastings

definitions.meaning: a humiliating snub or setback, as an idiom
King Harold is said to have been killed by an arrow striking his face at the Battle of Hastings in 1066

explanation.walkthrough: Hastings here is the 1066 battle where, by tradition (and the Bayeux Tapestry), the English king Harold was shot by an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a sharp humiliating setback, and literally describes the arrow wound legend gives the defeated English king.

clue.text: Mind the policy advocating destruction of america

parts.note: a protest slogan beginning 'No' calls for something to be done away with
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A remark about the mindset behind an anti-American campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as a slogan, 'No US', a policy calling for an end to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is common sense or intelligence, the practical faculty of the head.

clue.text: One on a small island

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone sits alone on a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hebridean isle is only a few miles long, a little island in Scottish waters.

clue.text: Sweets no longer on the menu in a Cumbrian course

indicators.note: the dish's word sits within the river's name, as one thing placed in another

parts.note: the River Tees rises on Cross Fell in Cumbria, a watercourse
a dish that has run out is 'off' in restaurant language

explanation.surface: Puddings have been struck off a menu during a meal in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' tempts as a meal course, but it is a watercourse: the Tees, a river of northern England rising in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffees are chewy confectionery made from boiled sugar and butter, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Spot Eastern man of intelligence

parts.note: a spy works in intelligence, gathering secrets

explanation.surface: Picking out an agent from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a literary synonym for noticing.

clue.text: Ely died somehow just gave up

indicators.note: says the letters are put together in some other, unstated way

explanation.surface: The cathedral city of Ely has died and surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ELY and DIED into the answer; 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yielded is to have surrendered or given way.

clue.text: Thirteen loafers nod off to a point

parts.note: bakers make loaves, so they are loaf-ers in a playful sense
to doze is to fall lightly asleep
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A count of idlers falling asleep with a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loafers' looks like idlers or shoes but is read as people who make loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker's dozen is an old trade custom of giving thirteen loaves for twelve.

clue.text: Fail to give sufficient emphasis when over worked?

definitions.meaning: to underplay or underemphasise a point or syllable
read as two words, a state of strain someone suffers when overworked

explanation.definitionFit: Understressing a word gives it too little weight; split in two, the phrase describes being strained by too much work.

clue.text: Not so colourful way to grovel

definitions.meaning: a pale light brown, a muted shade
to flatter servilely, as a dog does

explanation.definitionFit: Fawn is a soft beige colour, hardly vivid; as a verb it means to curry favour obsequiously.

clue.text: Nowhere else is high explosive planted by sappers

indicators.note: the explosive is set down beside the soldiers, so it comes next to them

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Military engineers have buried a bomb in this very spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; the Royal Engineers are abbreviated RE in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb points to this place and this place only, so it excludes anywhere else.

clue.text: Examination feared by all who want to add to their BA BSc

definitions.text: Examination feared by all who want to add to their BA BSc

parts.words: Examination feared by all who want to add to their BA BSc
parts.note: a gruelling police interrogation, disguised as a further university qualification after a first degree

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means harsh questioning by police; literally it would be a further academic qualification beyond two first degrees.

clue.text: Seek to parley if you can't afford to pay cash

definitions.meaning: to request negotiation, as a besieged force asks to discuss surrender

definitions.text: if you can't afford to pay cash
definitions.meaning: to request credit or instalment arrangements from a seller

explanation.definitionFit: Asking for terms means requesting conditions of surrender in war, or payment by instalments in a shop.

clue.text: Holster specially shaped for a horseman

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new form, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A gun holster made to fit a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially shaped' rearranges HOLSTER; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostler, or ostler, is a stableman who looks after horses at an inn.

clue.text: Events of course studied by anthropologists

definitions.meaning: contests run on a racecourse
human groups sharing ancestry, a subject of older anthropology

explanation.definitionFit: Meetings at a racecourse are contests of speed; ethnic groupings of humankind were classified by early anthropologists.

clue.text: Classic horse ideal for hunting flying foxes?

definitions.text: Classic horse ideal for hunting flying foxes?

parts.words: Classic horse ideal for hunting flying foxes?
parts.note: a winged steed of Greek myth, which could follow airborne quarry such as fruit bats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' suggests a racing Classic like the Derby, but means classical mythology; flying foxes are large fruit bats, so a hunter would need a mount that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek legend sprang from Medusa's blood and was ridden by Bellerophon.

clue.text: Horse waiting outside the maternity ward?

definitions.meaning: a harness horse that moves both legs on one side together
one who walks up and down nervously, as expectant fathers traditionally did

explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a trotting-race horse with a lateral gait, and also someone who walks to and fro anxiously.

clue.text: Salvation Army lassie's escort provides cold meal

parts.note: a lass goes out with a lad, her young man

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army girl's companion brings a chilled supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad is a dish of raw greens and vegetables, served chilled as a light repast.

clue.text: Vessel right behind as a sailor would say

parts.words: behind as a sailor would say
parts.note: aft is the nautical word for towards the stern

explanation.surface: A ship is directly astern, in naval parlance.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating platform, a simple craft for crossing water.

clue.text: Woolley's expression on making his famous archaeological discovery? Hardly

definitions.text: Woolley's expression on making his famous archaeological discovery? Hardly

parts.words: Woolley's expression on making his famous archaeological discovery? Hardly
parts.note: an exclamation of 'look!' before the ancient Sumerian city he excavated, yet as a word it is a scowl, hardly the face of a delighted digger

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Leonard Woolley excavated the Sumerian city of Ur in the 1920s; 'Lo, Ur!' would be his cry, but as one word it means a frown, so 'Hardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour is to look sullen or threatening, a gloomy facial look the excited archaeologist would not wear.

clue.text: Turn to, though if you turn too it's just the same

indicators.text: if you turn too it's just the same
indicators.note: turning the word round leaves it unchanged, so it reads identically both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Consulting something gives the same result however you spin it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn to' is the definition, as in consulting a book; 'turn too' then asks the solver to reverse the word, which changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to a source is to consult it or look in it.

clue.text: Temporary relief from ceremony which includes telepathic phenomena

indicators.note: the ceremony holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a rite is a ritual ceremony

explanation.surface: A seance-like ritual brings a short break from cares.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or pause from something difficult.

clue.text: Raise trading price by producing still finer nutmeg?

definitions.meaning: to buy up goods and sell them on at a profit in the same market
read as ..., to shred the spice again so it becomes finer

explanation.definitionFit: Regrating was the old offence of buying and reselling in the same market at a markup; split, it means shredding spice a second time.

clue.text: Handcuffs for devoted old husbands

definitions.meaning: old slang for manacles
after Darby and Joan, the proverbially loyal elderly couple

explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are a proverbial devoted old married couple in an 18th-century English ballad; a darby is such a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Darbies is old slang for shackles, and the plural of the faithful old husband in the ballad couple.

clue.text: Resume habit to make amends

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to put clothing on again
to put right a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Redress means to right a wrong or compensate; split, it means clothing oneself again.

clue.text: An air of merriment

definitions.meaning: a part-song for three or more voices, a tune
high spirits and delight

explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied English part-song, and the word also means great delight.

clue.text: Herb to make money

definitions.meaning: an aromatic garden plant used in sauces
to strike coins

explanation.definitionFit: Mint is an aromatic plant, and to mint is to stamp coinage.

clue.text: Put up a stake which last went up in Sicily in 197

definitions.text: which last went up in Sicily in 197

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: an ante is a poker player's stake paid before the deal

explanation.surface: A gambler raises the stakes on something that erupted in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the Sicilian volcano by its last eruption before the puzzle appeared (the year is cut short in the text held).
explanation.definitionFit: The volcano on Sicily's east coast erupts frequently, so it 'went up' in the year named.

clue.text: Harbour passed after dinner

definitions.meaning: a haven for ships
the fortified wine traditionally passed to the left round the table

explanation.definitionFit: A port is a haven for ships, and also the fortified Portuguese wine handed round after a formal meal.

clue.text: A case non-military engagement

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit in a non-criminal court
read literally, a battle fought by citizens rather than soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: A civil action is a lawsuit between private parties; literally it is a fight that is not military.

clue.text: Trees seen in Helmstedt

indicators.note: the letters can be spotted inside the German town's name

explanation.surface: Trees spotted in the German town of Helmstedt.
explanation.definitionFit: Elms are tall deciduous hardwoods.

clue.text: Political group celebrating establishment of social complex?

definitions.meaning: a moderate party between left and right
a celebration opening a new community hub

explanation.definitionFit: A centre party is a moderate political faction; literally, a party might mark the opening of a community building.
